newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower on overhead origin selling. January gave up $14 to close at $1,314 per tonne while March closed $17 lower at $1,258 per tonne. The January/March switch was active and accounted for most of the day's volume. Traders kept a close watch on reports of a cold airmass which some forecasters said could cause freezing temperatures and possible damage to the Mexican coffee belt later this week.

In New York the December contract expired today at a strong premium to March. Early on the market fell under last minute liquidation pressure, but was able to rebound. Early weakness across the board stemmed from the gains in the CSCE weekly warehouse figures, the GCA monthly figures and LIFFE daily figures yesterday.

The ability of the market to rally back was probably the result of a possible freeze in Mexico, although traders said it seems latest forecasts showed the heart of the coffee areas will probably be spared any damage from the cold temperatures expected later this week. It was added that although Mexico produces only about 5 per cent of world output that country does ship heavily to the United States and is of increased importance because it is not a member of the ACPC and therefore shipments are not restricted.

The outlook remains uncertain. While some traders believe the tight spot supply situation will spill over, bolstering March's premium to May, other traders said increased availability of Central American and Colombian coffees should ease supply concerns.

HONDURAS -The Honduran coffee crop has apparantly escaped major damage from the severe flooding that hit the country's north coast in mid-November and destroyed thousands of farmland hectares, the USDA agriculture attache in Honduras said. As a result, overall coffee production in Honduras in 1996/97 (October/September) is still expected to approach 2.5 million 60-kg bags up from 2.254 million bags the previous year, the attache said. It was added that the Honduran coffee institute recently made $769,000 available for the repair of flood-damaged roads and bridges that are crucial to coffee transport.

UGANDA - Coffee exports in November 1996 rose by 28 per cent while the export value increased by 21 per cent compared to the previous month, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said. 436,251 60-kg bags of coffee worth $32.57 million were exported in November, up from 340,451 bags valued at $26.82 million in October.

The rise in the export value despite the decline in world coffee prices is attributed to a 94 per cent increase in volume during the month. Total exports in the first two months of the 1996/97 coffee year (October/November) reached 776,702 bags valued at $59.4 million, up from 400,173 bags valued at $47.6 million, registered in the corresponding period last year.

The increased volumes at the start of the season were attributed to the inverted market which has discouraged hoarding of stocks at all levels within the marketing chain, UCDA said. This resulted in the liquidation of old stocks and the front-loading of the new crop.

ITALY - Italy imported 518,320 bags of coffee in May 1996, 3.2 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.485 million bags, nearly 8 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell slightly by 1.6 per cent to 5.387 million bags.
Main suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Zaire (227,900 vs 320,600 bags), Brazil (549,700 vs 644,900 bags), Colombia (183,000 vs 129,300 bags) and India (197,200 vs 170,800 bags).
The country exported 331,200 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 21 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose by 5.2 per cent to 738,900 bags.
